metadata.query: What happened between Verstappen and Hamilton at Turn 4 during the 2021 Brazilian GP?

data.query: What happened between Verstappen and Hamilton at Turn 4 during the 2021 Brazilian GP?
data.summary:
During the **2021 Brazilian (São Paulo) Grand Prix** on **November 14, 2021**, a major flashpoint occurred on **Lap 48** at Turn 4 (Descida do Lago) between championship rivals Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen [1.3, 1.4]:

### 1. The On-Track Incident (Lap 48)
Hamilton (Mercedes) used DRS to pull alongside Verstappen (Red Bull) on the run down the back straight, attempting an overtake around the outside of Turn 4 [1.7]. Verstappen, defending the inside line, braked extremely late and ran wide [1.3, 1.10]. Both cars failed to make the corner and were forced completely off the track into the asphalt run-off area, with Verstappen retaining the lead [1.3, 1.4]. No contact was made [1.3].

### 2. The Stewards' Initial Decision
The FIA Stewards noted the incident but decided **no investigation was necessary**, allowing Verstappen to escape penalty during the race [1.3, 1.7]. Race Director Michael Masi subsequently revealed that the stewards made this decision without access to Verstappen's forward-facing onboard camera footage, which was not broadcast live or available to them in real-time [1.2, 1.10].

### 3. Drivers' Perspectives
*   **Max Verstappen:** Defended his move as "fair, hard racing," adding, "we were fighting hard, braking late into the corner... If I would have turned more abrupt to the left, you'd just spin off the track.” [1.4]
*   **Lewis Hamilton:** Expressed sarcasm toward the decision but regrouped and successfully overtook Verstappen on Lap 59 to win the Grand Prix [1.3, 1.4].

### 4. Right of Review (FIA Regulations)
On November 16, 2021—following the post-race release of Verstappen's forward-facing onboard footage—Mercedes filed a petition for a **Right of Review under Article 14.1.1 of the FIA International Sporting Code (ISC)** [1.4, 1.5]. They argued the newly available footage constituted "significant and relevant new evidence" showing Verstappen opening his steering wheel to run Hamilton off [1.4, 1.10].

On November 19, 2021, the stewards officially **denied the petition**, concluding that while the footage was indeed "new" and "unavailable" at the time, it was not "significant" enough to justify reopening the case [1.2].
